name: Archaeology, Technology, and Historical Structures (Track B)
notes: ATHS integrates archaeology, architecture, classics, art history, the history of technology, and engineering. Once accepted into the program students are assigned an ATHS faculty advisor, chosen for fit with the student's interests in consultation with the program director.

TWO TRACKS: Track A is course-focused (eleven courses), Track B is research-focused (nine courses plus an eight-credit senior project). Both require a minimum of 44 credit hours. Each track is a separate entry here.
The three foundation courses - one each from engineering, archaeology and architecture - must be completed by the end of the fifth semester.

COURSE LISTS ARE STALE - NEEDS VERIFICATION: the department's course-categories page still carries notes like 'taught by visiting faculty in fall 2014' and 'Formerly CLA 220', and roughly a third of the course numbers it lists are absent from the 2025-26 catalog (among them ME 107/107W, ME 108, ME 207, ME 208, AHST 107/107W, AHST 150, AHST 201, AHST 243/243W, AHST 245, CLST 230W, CLST 231W, CLST 250/250W, CLST 299, HIST 162, HIST 207, HIST 299, EESC 215). They are kept as options because the department lists them, but check the term schedule and your advisor before planning around any of them.
ME 104Q on the department page is the catalog's ME 104 (The Engineering of Bridges); both codes are accepted.

Several courses are cross-listed and either code counts: ANTH 253 = HIST 217; ANTH 254 = HIST 218 = RELC 250; ITAL 223 = AHST 226 = CLST 223; ITAL 244 = AHST 244; AHST 394 = SART 394. ITAL 223 and ITAL 244 are taught in the Arezzo Program.
ME 394, CLST 394 and AHST/SART 394 internships require special approval.
Electives may be drawn from the elective list OR from any of the four core lists.

TRACK B (research-focused) requires nine courses plus an eight-credit senior project: three foundation courses, three core courses (at least two of them from the same core), three elective courses, and the senior project taken over two semesters.
Track B satisfies the upper-level writing requirement by writing the senior thesis/project report rather than by taking two W courses, so no ULW coursework is encoded here.
